request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The infant was admitted for surgical reduction of idiopathic ileocolic intussusception. She experienced postoperative ileus and later developed bilious vomiting on postoperative day seven, which prompted an abdominal x-ray and ultrasound that revealed ileoileal intussusception. The patient successfully underwent a laparotomy procedure where an ileoileal intussusception was manually reduced, with subsequent resection of a short necrotic segment. Following the procedure, the patient progressed well with no further complications. After satisfactory recovery, the patient was discharged home.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:
Not Applicable 

Discharge Instructions:
The patient should be monitored for any recurrent symptoms and advised to follow up with pediatric surgery as recommended. If any unusual symptom or behavior is observed, parents or family members should obtain medical advice immediately.

Follow-Up:
The patient should be accompanied by a responsible adult for routine follow-up and progress monitoring with pediatric surgery as recommended. 

Signed By:
[Redacted], M.D.
Date and Time: [Redacted]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
Chapter: the condition is intestinal intussusception, a disease of the digestive system, so the letter is **K**.

Category: in ICD-10-AM, intussusception is classified under **K56**, paralytic ileus and intestinal obstruction without hernia (the full code is K56.1, intussusception).

Principal diagnosis: the infant was admitted for surgical reduction of idiopathic ileocolic intussusception. That condition was chiefly responsible for the admission. The postoperative ileus and the later ileoileal intussusception arose during the stay. These are complications that would be coded as additional diagnoses, possibly as a postprocedural intestinal obstruction (K91.3), not as the principal diagnosis.

CODE: K56
